title: Los Angeles weather: Fire danger rises as Santa Ana winds, heat move into Southern California - ABC7 Los Angeles
text:
Los Angeles weather: Fire danger rises as Santa Ana winds, heat move into Southern California - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Weather 
 Fire danger rises as Santa Ana winds, heat move into SoCal 
 Santa Ana winds, low humidity and hotter temperatures are bringing elevated fire danger to Southern California. Saturday, November 7, 2026 3:18PM Share Follow ABC7 on Google Este artículo se ofrece en Español LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- Santa Ana winds, low humidity and hotter temperatures are bringing elevated fire danger to Southern California.
 Several parts of Los Angeles County will be under a red flag warning from 2 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturday. Those areas include the Santa Clarita Valley, Santa Monica Mountains, Santa Susana Mountains and western San Gabriel Mountains, including the Highway 14 corridor.
 During the peak of the wind event, gusts of 30 to 45 mph will be common in the typical wind-prone areas of Los Angeles and Ventura counties, according to the National Weather Service.
 The NWS also issued coastal alerts as high tides are expected.
 A beach hazard statement will be in effect through Tuesday morning along the coast of Ventura and L.A. counties. High tides of 7.2 to 7.6 feet are expected each morning. Expect 3 to 6 feet surf.
 The Orange County coast will be under a coastal flood advisory through noon Tuesday. The weather service said high tide is expected to peak at 7.4 to 7.6 feet Sunday and Monday. Surf will also increase.
 Weekend weather
 Los Angeles and Orange counties can expect a high of 88 degrees with a low of 58 on Saturday. There will be elevated fire danger. It could hit 90 degrees on Sunday.
 The valleys and the Inland Empire will also see increased fire risk, along with a high of 88 degrees and a low of 55 on Saturday. Sunday's high temperature will be around 90.
 Beach communities can expect sunny conditions on Saturday, with a high of 82 degrees and a low of 62. Conditions will be slightly warmer Sunday.
 Mountain areas will see sunny skies on Saturday, with a high of 60 degrees and a low of 32. Windy conditions should die down by Sunday.
 Deserts are expected to reach a high of 76 degrees and a low of 41 on Saturday. Palm Springs is expected to reach a high of 85 degrees. Similar weather is on tap Sunday.
